plan.reason: The PR adds an optional priority filter to GET /api/todos. Coverage gaps are the repository `where` branch (repository.ts:9) and the router 422 branch (router.ts:15). Existing tests assert only the unfiltered path, so none would catch a dropped or mis-forwarded filter.

cases.behavior: list({priority}) restricts the Prisma query to that priority and keeps newest-first ordering.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json GET /api/todos query parameter 'priority' ("Filter tasks by priority."); TodoListQuery type
cases.inputs: repository.list({ priority: 'high' }) with findMany mocked to resolve [record]
cases.expected: findMany called with { where: { priority: 'high' }, orderBy: [{ created_at: 'desc' }, { id: 'desc' }] }; result equals [todo]
cases.assertion: toHaveBeenCalledWith exact object including where and orderBy; mapped result toEqual [todo]
cases.mockBoundary: vi.spyOn(database.todo, 'findMany') on the real Prisma delegate; no database

existingTests.name: lists tasks in newest-first order and maps database rows

value.regression: The filter is ignored (no where clause), the where uses the wrong field, or ordering is dropped when filtering, so all priorities are returned.
value.rationale: The existing test only covers the no-query call and its exact-object assertion implies no where key, but nothing exercises the new branch (repository.ts:9 uncovered). One cheap case justifies the setup.

cases.behavior: GET /api/todos?priority=high passes the parsed query to repository.list; without a query it passes an empty filter.
cases.expected: First call list({ priority: 'high' }) with status 200 and body [todo]; second call list({}) with no priority key
cases.assertion: toHaveBeenCalledWith({ priority: 'high' }) and toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({}); the existing calledOnce check is strengthened
cases.mockBoundary: vi.fn() repository stub via the existing setup(); supertest on an express app

value.regression: The router drops req.query or forwards the raw/unvalidated query, so the repository never receives the priority filter.
value.rationale: The existing test asserts only calledOnce, so it cannot tell whether the query reaches the repository. Strengthening the same test costs almost nothing.

cases.behavior: An invalid priority query returns 422 with validation issues and does not call the repository.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json GET /api/todos response '422' (Invalid input) and priority enum
cases.expected: Status 422, body.detail is a non-empty array, repository.list not called
cases.assertion: status toBe 422; Array.isArray(detail) and length > 0; list not.toHaveBeenCalled

existingTests.name: rejects invalid create input without calling the repository: %j

value.regression: The 422 branch is removed or the enum is loosened, so an invalid priority reaches the repository, returning 200 or an unfiltered list.
value.rationale: The new 422 branch (router.ts:15) is uncovered, and the OpenAPI document promises it. An it.each over the three invalid values follows the existing create-validation test.

cases.behavior: listQuerySchema accepts an omitted priority and each enum value, and rejects values outside the enum.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json priority enum low|medium|high, required false
cases.expected: {} parses to {}; each valid value parses to itself; 'urgent' and '' fail
cases.assertion: parse toEqual for valid inputs; safeParse(...).success toBe(false) for invalid ones

existingTests.name: accepts every input field and boundary lengths

value.regression: The priority is made required, the enum is widened to any string, or a valid value is rejected.
value.rationale: validators.ts has a 100% per-file coverage threshold, and the existing validator tests never import listQuerySchema. Direct schema tests are cheap and pin the contract independently of Express.

remainingGaps: backend/openapi.json content (parameter enum and 422 response) is not asserted; the factory test stubs the spec, so a document-content test would need a supplied contract.
Unknown query keys being stripped (e.g. ?foo=bar) is unconfirmed characterization of z.object; not planned.
Repeated priority query params (array values) behaviour is unspecified; left out.
Frontend has no use of the new priority filter in this PR; frontend coverage gaps are unrelated to the diff.
backend/src/factory.ts:20 and backend/src/main.ts are pre-existing gaps outside this change.
